questions.q: State the NCERT definition of "growth" and "development" and give one example where growth occurs without development.
questions.a: Growth is quantitative and value-neutral (can be positive or negative); development is qualitative and always value-positive. Example: A city's population doubles (growth) but housing, sanitation, and schools remain unchanged, so quality of life declines (no development). A wrong answer that equates growth with development reveals the student has not internalised the value-neutral vs value-positive distinction.

questions.q: Why does the NCERT say "positive growth does not always lead to development"? Explain using the city population example from the textbook.
questions.a: Positive growth (population increase) only adds numbers; development requires qualitative improvement in services and opportunities. If infrastructure and services do not expand proportionally, the same facilities are shared by more people, reducing per-capita access. A wrong answer that claims growth automatically brings development shows the student misses the conditional link: development occurs only when growth is accompanied by investment in human capabilities.

questions.q: Two Indian states, A and B, have identical per capita income (₹2,00,000). State A has life expectancy 75 years and literacy 95%; State B has life expectancy 65 years and literacy 70%. Using the capability approach, which state has higher human development? Justify in three steps.
questions.a: Step 1: Recognise that the capability approach values health and education as intrinsic capabilities, not just income. Step 2: Compare health capability — State A's 75-year life expectancy indicates better healthcare, nutrition, and disease control. Step 3: Compare education capability — State A's 95% literacy means far greater access to knowledge and skill formation. Conclusion: State A has higher human development despite equal income. A wrong answer that picks based on income alone reveals the student still defaults to the income approach.

questions.q: Analyse the following statement: "Kerala has lower per capita income than Gujarat but higher HDI rank. This proves economic growth is irrelevant for human development." Identify the logical flaw and correct the interpretation.
questions.a: The flaw is treating the relationship as binary. Kerala's higher HDI shows that income is not the sole determinant; it does not prove income is irrelevant. Correct interpretation: Kerala converts its moderate income into better health/education outcomes through high social-sector spending, equitable distribution, and historical investments in public services. A wrong answer that agrees with the statement shows the student cannot distinguish "not the only factor" from "not a factor at all".

questions.q: Evaluate the welfare approach versus the capability approach for addressing child malnutrition in a tribal district. Which approach better empowers the community long-term? Give two reasons.
questions.a: The capability approach is superior. Reason 1: Welfare approach delivers food supplements (passive receipt), while capability approach builds mothers' knowledge, healthcare access, and livelihood skills (active agency). Reason 2: Capability approach addresses root causes (education, gender equity, forest rights) making gains sustainable; welfare approach creates dependency on state transfers. A wrong answer favouring welfare approach reveals the student confuses short-term relief with long-term development.

questions.q: Design a village-level indicator dashboard that captures human development beyond economic growth. List five indicators, explain why each reflects a capability, and specify the data source for each.
questions.a: Good answer includes: (1) Under-5 mortality rate (health capability) — NFHS data; (2) Mean years of schooling for women (education capability) — Census/ASER; (3) Percentage of households with piped water (resource access capability) — Jal Jeevan Mission MIS; (4) Youth unemployment rate (economic opportunity capability) — PLFS; (5) Women's participation in Gram Sabha (political freedom capability) — Panchayat records. A poor answer lists only income or infrastructure indicators, showing the student cannot operationalise the capability concept.
